$comment: Human-approved exceptions to a gate.sh check. TRO-553 built this after G6
(regression-test) failed three real docs-only/test-only tickets whose
premise — every ticket changes production code — does not hold for them.
The mechanism is generic over the gate id, not G6-specific: gate.sh calls
the same check_gate_exception function from both G6 and G8, and TRO-542's
entry below is a live G8 (eval-not-regressed) instance.
RULES:
(1) Only the orchestrator writes an entry here, and only after Troy's
approval already exists on the named Linear ticket. An agent must
never add its own entry — that would be self-approval.
(2) gate.sh honors an entry ONLY when "approver" is a non-empty string.
An entry with an empty or missing approver reads as unapproved, and
the gate still fails — see scripts/factory/gate-exceptions.ts.
(3) gate.sh reads THIS FILE FROM BASE_REF, never from the ticket branch's
own working copy (see gate.sh, next to the quarantine baseline it
copies the same discipline from). Editing this file on a ticket
branch has ZERO effect on that ticket's own gate run — rule (1) is
then code-enforced, not only documented: an entry only takes effect
once the commit adding it has already landed on the base branch.
(4) One entry exempts one ticket from one named gate id. It does not
exempt the ticket from any other gate, and it does not carry over to
a different ticket that happens to touch the same files.
Schema per entry: ticket (TRO-nnn), gate (the gate.sh check id), reason
(why this gate cannot pass honestly right now), approver (a name; empty
means NOT approved), date (YYYY-MM-DD the approval was given), pr
(optional — the PR this exception covers, for provenance; omitted when
the approval is not tied to one specific PR).

Compounded by 31-vs-32-case corpus drift (TRO-556). TRO-561 is the systemic fix; this exception covers the interim.
